policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere lezawah and ketiv lz'wh are orthographic variants of the same noun from z-w-' (trembling, horror). ASV 'to be tossed to and fro' with the note 'Or, a terror' renders that sense either way, and the note is classed alternative_rendering, so it is about English wording and cannot decide a reading. Nothing in the English distinguishes the two spellings; base qere fallback carries the projection.
ASV transliterates 'Jeuel', which reflects the ketiv y'w'l (Jeuel); the qere y'y'l would give 'Jeiel'. The English name form distinguishes the readings and matches the ketiv.
ASV transliterates 'Jehuel', which reflects the ketiv yhw'l; the qere yhy'l would give 'Jehiel'. The English name form distinguishes the readings and matches the ketiv.

Qere mahtzerim and ketiv mahtzetzerim are spellings of the same hiphil participle of hatzotzer, 'to sound a trumpet'. ASV 'the trumpeters sounded' renders that participle and does not distinguish the two spellings; no note is mapped here. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
